nodes.label: SPA shell
nodes.rationale: Minimal shell: a 64x64 favicon link, the viewport meta, a #root mount point and the main.tsx module.

nodes.label: Vite React template notes
nodes.source_location: Stock Vite template README covering the two React plugins and Oxlint rules; not project-specific.

nodes.label: Vercel frontend deployment
nodes.rationale: VITE_* variables are inlined at build time, so a variable change needs a redeploy to take effect.

nodes.label: Backend CI job
nodes.rationale: Builds the Docker test stage, which compiles and runs the unit suite, then builds the runtime image.

nodes.label: Frontend CI job
nodes.rationale: npm ci, lint, Vitest and a production build with tsc; a red check blocks the merge.

nodes.label: Supabase service-role key committed in docker-compose.yml
nodes.norm_label: supabase service-role key committed in docker-compose.yml
nodes.rationale: A live service_role JWT - full admin access to the Supabase project - is stored in a tracked file. It contradicts the secrets rules in OPERATIONS.md and the "no secret in source" finding of the security audit, and it needs rotation rather than deletion because the repository is public.

nodes.label: Configuration platform map
nodes.rationale: VITE_* variables are public and build-time on Vercel; everything else is server-only runtime configuration on Railway.

nodes.label: Documented configuration inconsistencies
nodes.rationale: docker-compose sets NEXUS_JWT_EXPIRATION_MINUTES that nothing reads, and /api/health is a static handler that stays green while Postgres is down - both are traps for a responder.

nodes.label: Release and verify flow
nodes.rationale: Both platforms deploy from main; a deploy that has not been verified is not done.

nodes.label: Layer-by-layer rollback
nodes.rationale: Frontend rollback is a promoted earlier deployment, backend rollback is a redeploy of an earlier build, and the database has nothing to revert because migrations are forward-only.

nodes.label: Railway backend deployment
nodes.rationale: A long-running container, not a serverless function - that is what keeps the chat and whiteboard WebSockets connected in production.

nodes.label: Nexus workspace platform
nodes.rationale: One workspace for planning, building, documenting and shipping: projects, sprints, board, backlog, wiki, inbox, calendar, analytics, whiteboard and a copilot share one data model, so the plan and the work never diverge.

nodes.label: Admin-provisioned accounts
nodes.rationale: There is no public signup: POST /api/auth/register is ADMIN-only, and seeded accounts sign in with a documented password until Supabase takes over the credential.

nodes.label: Nexus technology stack
nodes.rationale: React 19 + Vite frontend, Spring Boot 4.1 (Java 21) backend, Postgres 16 with Flyway, Redis 7 for whiteboard fan-out, optional Supabase Auth.

nodes.label: .env.example
nodes.rationale: Documents every environment variable; values are placeholders, never real secrets.

nodes.label: Applied migrations are immutable
nodes.rationale: Editing an applied migration makes Flyway fail checksum validation on the next boot, which takes the service down instead of rolling it back - a worse outcome than the bad column it was meant to fix.

nodes.label: Secrets handling rules
nodes.rationale: Keys live in platform dashboards, never in the repository. The Supabase anon key is public by design; the service-role key is full access and must never be prefixed with VITE_.

nodes.label: Public-site hygiene gap
nodes.rationale: Favicon and title exist; meta description, social preview, robots/sitemap, custom 404, skip link, cookie consent and privacy/terms pages do not.

nodes.label: Known gaps and next milestones
nodes.rationale: Self-declared gaps: client-side team grouping, no refresh-token rotation, a dev-only JWT fallback secret, per-instance rate limiting, and no browser-level E2E suite. Gaps 3 and 4 were addressed by the security pass recorded in SECURITY_AUDIT.md, so this section is now stale.

nodes.label: Declared request-body cap
nodes.rationale: A declared Content-Length over the cap is refused with 413 before the body is read; chunked requests are left to per-endpoint validation.

nodes.label: CORS tightening
nodes.rationale: Allowed headers narrowed to the four the API uses, with a single origin property feeding Spring CORS.

nodes.label: Recorded security defaults
nodes.rationale: Every hardening knob has an explicit default so a deployment can tighten it without a code change, and each choice is written down with its reasoning.

nodes.label: Generic error responses
nodes.rationale: The container error path never echoes internal messages or binding details; the API handler still returns field-level validation errors where they are useful.

nodes.label: Security headers policy
nodes.rationale: nosniff, DENY framing, referrer and permissions policy plus a CSP that blocks inline and third-party scripts while allowing the inline styles the SPA uses.

nodes.label: JWT secret fails fast
nodes.rationale: A shipped fallback secret is a public signing key for every deployment that forgets to set one; failing at startup is louder than a silently weak deployment.

nodes.label: Global and per-route rate limits
nodes.rationale: Auth keeps its stricter limit while a global per-IP window backs every other API route; counters are in-memory so the budget is per instance.

nodes.label: WebSocket frame bounds
nodes.rationale: An authenticated socket is still an untrusted client, so frames are size-bounded and the chat socket also has a per-window frame budget.

nodes.label: REST, SSE and WebSocket API surface
nodes.norm_label: rest, sse and websocket api surface
nodes.rationale: One table of every endpoint: REST for CRUD, SSE for streamed AI answers, and JWT-authenticated WebSocket paths for chat and whiteboard.

nodes.label: Hybrid retrieval with rank fusion
nodes.rationale: Postgres full-text plus keyword plus vector ranking, fused; only a small context package is sent, so a question never costs a whole-database read.

nodes.label: Knowledge chunk index
nodes.rationale: Wiki, project, task, sprint and whiteboard records are chunked with metadata and an embedding, then re-indexed incrementally after each commit so the index tracks the data.

nodes.label: Nexus AI retrieval-augmented chat
nodes.rationale: A second AI surface at /ai with its own /api/ai endpoints, kept alongside the grounded Copilot rather than replacing it.

nodes.label: Workspace role model
nodes.rationale: ADMIN changes roles; MEMBER and DEVELOPER write; VIEWER is read-only intent enforced at the API by annotations rather than by the UI.

nodes.label: VIEWER read-only enforcement
nodes.rationale: Read-only has to be enforced per endpoint, otherwise a management rule accidentally becomes "members cannot work" or a viewer can still write.

nodes.label: Redis whiteboard fan-out
nodes.rationale: Redis pub/sub carries whiteboard events between backend instances with origin tagging, so one instance never replays its own echo.

nodes.label: Single data model vision
nodes.rationale: Small teams juggle 3-5 disconnected tools and the plan drifts from the work; one shared data model is the product bet that prevents the drift.

nodes.label: Grounded Copilot answers
nodes.rationale: Deterministic answers computed from live workspace data keep the feature useful with no API key and no external call, so an unconfigured or failing provider degrades quality instead of breaking the page.
